text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said the richest should pay most taxes.
- Portugal's inflation rate harmonised with the other European Union (EU) states was 2.3 percent in March, down from 2.4 percent in February and half a percentage point above the EU average.
- Special bank savings accounts introduced two months ago for the privatisation of EDP - Electricidade de Portugal have already attracted deposits of 120 billion escudos.

- Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said at yesterday's Ecofin summit in Brussels that even if Portugal's economy grew at one percent below official forecasts, the budget deficit would be under the target of three percent. Some EU partners had said Portugal's GDP growth forecasts were too optimistic.
- Manuel Carvalho da Silva, head of trade union group CGTP, said 600,000 workers were benefiting from a reduction of working hours due to a law enforcing a 40-hour working week.
